newsitem.title: USA: No death penalty sought in Cosby murder case.
newsitem.headline: No death penalty sought in Cosby murder case.

text.p: Prosecutors said on Friday they would not seek the death penalty against the man accused of murdering the only son of entertainer Bill Cosby.
At a hearing in Los Angeles, they told the judge they would not press for "special circumstances" or capital punishment against Mikhail Markhasev, an 18-year-old Ukrainian immigrant.
Markhasev has been charged with the Jan. 16 murder of Ennis Cosby, who was shot while changing a flat tyre by the side of a Los Angeles freeway. He pleaded not guilty at arraignment this month.
California law allows for capital punishment in cases where a murder occurs during commission of a robbery.
Police have said they believe Markhasev was trying either to steal Cosby's expensive Mercedes-Benz car or to rob him to get money for drugs.
At Friday's hearing, the judge ruled that the murder trial would take place in Santa Monica and that the next hearing would be on June 12.
